concepts.learning_objective: Define life processes as the maintenance functions of an organism and name nutrition, respiration, transportation and excretion.
Explain why invisible molecular movement is needed to repair and maintain living structures.
Explain why diffusion is insufficient for multicellular organisms and why specialised tissues and transport are needed.
Describe the raw materials, events and products of photosynthesis and how plants store unused carbohydrate.
Interpret the starch-test activities showing that chlorophyll and carbon dioxide are essential for photosynthesis.
Explain how guard cells open and close stomata and how plants obtain water and minerals such as nitrogen.

topics.title: Heterotrophic nutrition and nutrition in single-celled organisms

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between organisms that break down food outside the body, those that take in whole food, and parasites.
Describe how Amoeba and Paramoecium take in and digest food.
Explain the roles of teeth, saliva, gastric glands, acid, pepsin and mucus in digestion.
Explain how bile, pancreatic juice and intestinal juice complete the digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats.
Explain how villi absorb digested food and how the large intestine absorbs water.
Compare the pathways by which glucose is broken down in yeast, in muscle cells and in mitochondria.
Describe ATP as the energy currency of the cell and how it is made and used.
Explain gaseous exchange in plants, aquatic animals and the human respiratory system.
Trace the flow of blood through the four chambers of the heart and explain double circulation.
Distinguish arteries, veins and capillaries and interpret systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
Describe the roles of platelets in clotting and of lymph in transport.
Explain why plants need a transport system and why it can be relatively slow.
Explain how root pressure and transpiration pull move water and minerals up the xylem.
Describe translocation of food in phloem and how it uses energy from ATP.

topics.title: Excretion in human beings and plants

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the organs of the human excretory system and the path of urine.
Explain filtration and selective reabsorption in nephrons and compare the kidney with dialysis.
Describe the ways in which plants get rid of their waste products.
